messages:
elaine: Quick alert — after the 2026-03-17 runtime push we're seeing a regression on a subset of Mixtral/Qwen workloads. p95 latency doubled on long-chat traces (>1024 tokens) and we're seeing repeated fallback churn between FlashAttention and SDPA/Triton. Root logs show weird mask compatibility failures for certain head_dim values.
marc: Ugh. Do we have a repro script and a kernel decision trace? pinging @priya for profiling artifacts.
priya: I ran a focused repro on mixtral-7b-custom (weird head dims) and captured the runtime kernel selection log + perf counters. Snippet below from the router logs:

```
[2026-03-17T18:04:12Z] model=mixtral-7b variant=fp16 head_dim=77 seq=1536 selected_kernel=flash_attn status=OK
[2026-03-17T18:04:12Z] model=mixtral-7b variant=fp16 head_dim=77 seq=1536 fallback_to=sdpa reason=mask_stride_mismatch mask_bitwidth=8
[2026-03-17T18:04:12Z] kernel_latency_ms.flash=2.3 kernel_latency_ms.sdpa=4.8 kv_cache_ops=+0.12% cache_miss_rate=13.4%
```

priya: Note head_dim 77 is deliberately from a trimmed checkpoint we have in staging. FlashAttention chooses a fast path but then the mask check fails mid-compile and we see fallback. The fallback path is much slower for our latency-sensitive routing, and batching amplifies cost.
nick: Interesting — does the mask check compare bitwidth or alignment? We recently changed some RoPE scaling logic that touches mask generation for long sequences.
priya: The failure looks like a small mismatch: mask generation for 1024+ sequences uses a uint8 mask in one code path and a 32-bit mask in another. When batching mixes small and long sequences we end up calling the flash kernel with an incompatible mask layout.
sophie: Also saw KV cache offset weirdness in traces: when mixing cached-prefix requests with full-context requests the KV indices shift for the third request in the batch. Small repro below (log slices):

```
[req1] batch_idx=0 kv_write.start=0 kv_write.end=1024
[req2] batch_idx=1 kv_write.start=1024 kv_write.end=2048
[req3] batch_idx=2 kv_write.start=1023 kv_write.end=2047   <-- off-by-one
```

sophie: That off-by-one plus the mask mismatch explains corrupt attention weights and triggers safeties that force fallback to SDPA/Triton.
marc: Okay this feels like two related issues: (A) mask layout/bitwidth inconsistency across codepaths (maybe introduced in the RoPE scaling refactor) and (B) a KV batching index bug when compacting variable-length KV buffers. Both cause kernel incompatibility and force fallback.
elaine: Any quick mitigations we can deploy? Canary rollback? Or runtime gate to force SDPA for suspicious combos to avoid churn?
priya: Short-term: add a conservative compatibility check in kernel selector: if head_dim % 8 != 0 or mask_layout != expected -> pick SDPA deterministically (no mid-call fallback). That avoids churn but costs latency. I can push a patch today.
nick: Also suggest adding a tiny unit test in the batching harness that mixes cached and non-cached requests with varying seq lengths — should catch the kv offset regression. I'll draft one.
sophie: For long term we should unify mask generation to always emit 32-bit masks for flash paths, and ensure the kernel compile-time probe validates mask stride/bitwidth before enqueuing kernels.
marc: Agreed. Action items: priya will open a PR with conservative selector + logging; nick will add batching unit tests; sophie will spec mask unification; I'll own an infra canary to roll the selector across a small subset of prod hosts.
elaine: Sounds good. Please add perf numbers in the PR description (before/after p50/p95/p99) and mark the canary route. I want observability to clearly show when fallback rate drops.
ops-bot: deploy-checklist created: /tickets/RT-2026-77 · canary group=shadow-io-3 · selector_patch=PR#4123
marc: One more: check behavior for Qwen variants — their head_dim packing is different (they often use 64 or 80) so we might not hit the same combo, but the mask/layout invariants must hold across models. Priya can run quick smoke across llama/mistral/qwen once the selector patch is available.
priya: Will do. Uploading the profiling tarball to the incident bucket now and will link in the PR. For the immediate canary I'll only enable the selector on dedicated GPUs in us-west2.
elaine: Thanks all. If anyone finds more repros drop them here. I'll update the incident board with the action items.
